name: Coal-fired power plant
also_called: coal plant; thermal power station; coal CHP
description: A power station that burns coal in boilers to raise steam for turbines.
visual_cues: Large boiler house next to a turbine hall; one or more tall chimney stacks with long shadows; dark coal stockpile yard with stacker-reclaimers; conveyor belts from the yard to the boilers; cooling towers or a cooling-water intake and outfall; flue-gas desulphurisation units (round absorbers) beside the stacks; grey ash ponds nearby; rail loop or jetty for coal delivery.

name: Open-pit coal mine
also_called: surface mine; strip mine; opencast mine; lignite mine
description: A coal mine where seams are reached by removing the overlying rock and soil from the surface.
visual_cues: Very large terraced excavation; dark exposed coal benches; haul roads with switchbacks; spoil (overburden) dumps; draglines or bucket-wheel excavators; dust; rail or conveyor load-out.

name: Underground coal mine (surface facilities)
description: The surface works of a coal mine whose seams are reached by shafts or drifts.
visual_cues: Headframes or winding towers over shafts; ventilation fan houses; coal preparation (washing) plant; small dark stockpiles; rail loading silos; slurry ponds; little visible excavation compared with open-pit mines; sometimes subsidence ponds in the surrounding area.

name: Coal preparation plant
description: A plant at or near a mine that crushes and washes coal to remove rock and ash.
visual_cues: Tall multi-storey plant building; conveyors radiating to raw and clean coal stockpiles; thickener tanks (round clarifiers); fine-reject (tailings) ponds; rail load-out silo or loop.

name: Coal stockpile / stockyard
description: An open-air area where coal is stored in long piles before use or shipping.
visual_cues: Long parallel black or dark grey piles; rail-mounted stacker-reclaimers running between them; conveyors; sometimes enclosed in long sheds or domes; found at power plants, ports, mines and steelworks.

name: Coal terminal
also_called: coal port; coal export terminal; coal import terminal
description: A port facility that loads or unloads coal to or from bulk carriers.
visual_cues: Coal stockyard on the shore; conveyor running along a long jetty or wharf; travelling ship loader or grab unloaders; bulk carriers moored alongside; rail loop or car dumper feeding the yard.

name: Coal ash pond
also_called: ash impoundment; ash dam; CCR pond
description: An impoundment where coal combustion residues are stored, often as a slurry.
visual_cues: Flat grey to light-brown basin enclosed by earthen dikes; pipes from the plant; patches of standing water; located next to or near a coal plant.

name: Onshore oil and gas field
description: An area of land where oil or gas is produced from many wells.
visual_cues: Regular grid or scatter of small cleared well pads joined by access roads; pumpjacks; gathering pipelines; small tank batteries and separators; central processing facility; flares; produced-water ponds.

name: Oil or gas well pad
description: A cleared area that holds one or more oil or gas wells.
visual_cues: Small rectangular cleared pad, often light-coloured gravel; pumpjacks or wellheads in a row; small tanks; a drilling rig casts a tall shadow while drilling; fracking pads show many trucks and tanks.

name: Offshore oil and gas platform
also_called: oil rig; production platform; jacket platform
description: A fixed structure at sea used to drill for or produce oil and gas.
visual_cues: Rectangular deck on legs in open water; helideck; flare boom; supply vessels nearby; sometimes several platforms joined by bridges; wake-free (does not move).

name: FPSO (floating production storage and offloading)
description: A ship-shaped vessel that produces, stores and offloads oil at an offshore field.
visual_cues: Tanker-like hull covered with process modules on deck; turret or spread mooring; flare tower at one end; a shuttle tanker sometimes moored astern; risers to the seabed.

name: Oil refinery
also_called: petroleum refinery; refining and petrochemical complex
description: An industrial plant that turns crude oil into fuels and other products.
visual_cues: Dense process units with distillation columns casting tall thin shadows; pipe racks; many storage tanks of different sizes; one or more flares; spheres for liquefied gases; sulphur piles at some sites; often next to a port or pipeline terminal.

name: Oil storage terminal
also_called: tank farm; tank terminal; crude storage
description: A group of large cylindrical tanks for storing crude oil or products.
visual_cues: Clusters of round tanks, often inside rectangular bunds (earth walls); floating-roof tanks show a crescent shadow inside the rim that changes with fill level; pipework and small pump houses between tanks; often at ports and pipeline ends.

name: Oil export / import terminal
description: A coastal facility where oil is loaded onto or unloaded from tankers.
visual_cues: Large tank farm on the shore; pipelines to a long jetty, sea island or offshore mooring buoys; tankers berthed or anchored nearby; pumping station.

name: Oil or NGL pipeline
also_called: crude pipeline; products pipeline; NGL pipeline
description: A pipeline carrying crude oil, refined products or natural gas liquids.
visual_cues: Usually buried: a straight cleared strip across fields or forest; above-ground in some deserts and permafrost (raised on supports); pumping stations at intervals; ends at terminals, refineries or tank farms.

name: Oil pipeline pumping station
description: A facility along an oil pipeline that keeps the oil moving.
visual_cues: Fenced site on a pipeline route with pump buildings, a few small tanks, and sometimes a small power supply; pipeline corridor entering and leaving.

name: Oil-fired power plant
also_called: diesel power plant; fuel-oil power station
description: A power station that burns fuel oil or diesel, in boilers, turbines or engines.
visual_cues: Fuel-oil storage tanks with bunds next to the power block; a stack or several small engine stacks; often on islands or coasts with a fuel jetty; looks like a gas or coal plant without a coal yard.

name: Gas-fired power plant (combined cycle)
description: A power station that burns gas in gas turbines and reuses the exhaust heat to make steam.
visual_cues: Compact layout with no fuel stockpile; heat-recovery steam generators (tall rectangular boxes) each with a short stack; turbine hall; air-cooled condenser (block of fans) or mechanical-draft cooling towers; small gas reception area; switchyard next to the plant.

name: Gas-fired power plant (open cycle)
description: A power station of gas turbines without steam recovery, used mainly at times of peak demand.
visual_cues: Rows of small turbine enclosures, each with its own short stack directly attached; no steam generators or cooling towers; small footprint; switchyard.

name: Gas engine power plant
description: A power station of many large gas (or dual-fuel) engines.
visual_cues: Long engine hall with a row of many identical small stacks; radiator coolers on the roof or beside the hall; small tanks; switchyard.

name: Gas processing plant
description: A facility that removes water, CO2, sulphur and liquids from raw natural gas.
visual_cues: Process units and pipe racks smaller than a refinery; a few tanks and spheres; flare; pipelines converging from surrounding well fields; sometimes yellow sulphur blocks.

name: Gas pipeline
description: A pipeline carrying natural gas (or hydrogen) over long distances.
visual_cues: Straight or gently curving cleared strip across fields or forest, with different vegetation colour; marker posts; valve stations and compressor stations at intervals; often runs beside roads or other pipelines; during construction, a wide bare strip with the pipe laid alongside a trench.

name: Gas compressor station
description: A facility along a gas pipeline that compresses the gas to keep it moving.
visual_cues: Fenced rectangle with one or more compressor buildings and short exhaust stacks; gas coolers (rows of fans); pipeline corridor entering and leaving; located at intervals of roughly 100–200 km along a pipeline.

name: Underground gas storage (surface facilities)
description: Surface plant of a site that stores gas underground in depleted fields, salt caverns or aquifers.
visual_cues: Compressor and treatment plant; scattered well pads connected by pipelines; for salt caverns, leaching ponds and brine pipelines.

name: Gas flare
description: A stack or pit where unwanted gas is burned.
visual_cues: Tall thin stack with a long shadow, or a ground flare pit or enclosed flare; scorched ground around it; visible flame or smoke in some images; common at refineries, LNG plants, processing plants and oil fields; easily seen at night and in infrared.

name: LNG export terminal
description: A plant that cools natural gas into liquid and loads it onto ships.
visual_cues: Long rectangular liquefaction trains of process equipment; large round white LNG storage tanks with domed roofs; flares; a jetty with loading arms; LNG carriers alongside; often a large cleared coastal site.

name: LNG import terminal
description: A facility that receives LNG from ships and turns it back into gas.
visual_cues: Large round LNG storage tanks; jetty with unloading arms; compact vaporiser area; no liquefaction trains; pipeline leaving the site.

name: LNG storage tank
description: A large insulated tank that holds LNG at about -160 °C.
visual_cues: Very large round tank (often 70–90 m across) with a white or light domed roof; concrete outer wall; stairs or pipe rack to the roof; usually in groups of two to four.

name: FSRU (floating storage and regasification unit)
description: A ship moored permanently at a jetty or buoy that stores LNG and turns it back into gas.
visual_cues: LNG-carrier-shaped vessel moored at a fixed jetty or offshore; regasification modules on deck near the bow; a trestle or pipeline to shore; usually no onshore tanks.

name: FLNG (floating liquefied natural gas vessel)
description: A very large vessel moored at an offshore field that liquefies gas at sea.
visual_cues: Very long hull covered with dense process modules; turret mooring at one end; flare tower; LNG carriers moored alongside to offload; far offshore.

name: LNG carrier
description: A ship that carries liquefied natural gas.
visual_cues: Long ship with either a row of large spherical domes (Moss type) or a flat raised trunk deck (membrane type); accommodation block at the stern; often seen at LNG terminals.

name: Solar PV farm
also_called: solar park; photovoltaic plant; utility-scale solar
description: A large array of photovoltaic panels that generates electricity.
visual_cues: Regular rows of dark blue or black panels; single-axis trackers show long north–south rows; fenced perimeter; access tracks between blocks; small inverter or transformer stations spread across the site; a substation at the edge.

name: Floating solar PV
description: Photovoltaic panels mounted on floats on a lake, reservoir or flooded mine.
visual_cues: Dark rectangular or irregular rafts of panels on water; walkways between blocks; anchored by lines to the shore; cable to an inverter station on the bank.

name: Rooftop and distributed solar
description: Solar panels on buildings, car parks and other small sites.
visual_cues: Dark rectangles of panels on factory, warehouse or house roofs; canopies over car parks; much smaller and more scattered than solar farms.

name: Concentrated solar power (tower)
description: A plant that uses a field of mirrors to focus sunlight on a receiver at the top of a tower.
visual_cues: Central tower with a very long shadow; circular or fan-shaped field of thousands of small mirrors (heliostats); power block with turbine and cooling; molten-salt storage tanks; in deserts.

name: Concentrated solar power (parabolic trough)
description: A plant that uses long rows of curved mirrors to heat a fluid that drives a turbine.
visual_cues: Long, perfectly straight parallel rows of curved mirrors that look bright or silver; central power block; thermal-storage tanks; in deserts.

name: Onshore wind farm
description: A group of wind turbines on land.
visual_cues: Turbines appear as small white dots with long thin shadows showing tower and blades; a cleared crane pad and access road to each turbine; turbines spaced in rows or along ridges; a substation nearby.

name: Offshore wind farm
description: A group of wind turbines at sea.
visual_cues: Regular grid of small white points on open water; wakes or shadows; an offshore substation platform; service vessels; export cable route to shore.

name: Hydropower dam (reservoir)
description: A dam that stores water and generates electricity as it flows through turbines.
visual_cues: Concrete or earth dam across a river valley; reservoir upstream; powerhouse at the base with outflow channels; spillway; switchyard and transmission lines leaving the site.

name: Run-of-river hydropower
description: A hydropower plant that uses the river's flow with little or no storage.
visual_cues: Low weir or barrage across a river; intake and a canal, tunnel portal or penstock; powerhouse downstream, sometimes kilometres away; small switchyard.

name: Pumped-storage hydropower
description: A hydropower plant that pumps water to an upper reservoir to store energy and releases it to generate.
visual_cues: Two reservoirs at very different heights, the upper one often an artificial basin on a hilltop with a lined rim; penstocks or tunnels between them; powerhouse at the lower reservoir; water level marks show daily cycling.

name: Geothermal power plant
description: A power station that uses steam or hot water from underground.
visual_cues: Scattered well pads linked by silver steam pipelines with zig-zag expansion loops; compact power house; cooling towers with white steam plumes; often in volcanic or hilly terrain.

name: Biomass power plant
also_called: biomass plant; wood-pellet power station; bagasse cogeneration
description: A power station that burns wood, crop waste or other biomass.
visual_cues: Like a small coal plant but with light-brown wood-chip or pellet piles, or large fuel storage domes; boiler house and stack; often at sawmills, pulp mills or sugar mills.

name: Biogas plant
description: A plant that makes gas from organic waste in digesters and often burns it in engines.
visual_cues: Round digester tanks, often with green or grey domed membrane roofs; silage clamps; slurry lagoons; small engine container; usually next to farms or wastewater plants.

name: Waste-to-energy plant
description: A plant that burns municipal waste to produce electricity and heat.
visual_cues: Large enclosed building with a waste bunker and truck ramp; one tall stack; flue-gas treatment; usually in or near cities; no outdoor fuel piles.

name: Battery energy storage system
description: A facility of battery units that stores electricity for the grid.
visual_cues: Rows of identical white shipping-container-sized units on a gravel pad; small inverter units; fenced; usually next to a substation, solar farm or power plant.

name: Nuclear power plant
description: A power station that uses nuclear fission to make steam for turbines.
visual_cues: Cylindrical reactor containment buildings, often with domed roofs; large turbine halls; very large natural-draft cooling towers or a cooling-water intake on a coast, lake or river; extensive security perimeter; switchyard.

name: Transmission line
description: An overhead high-voltage line carrying electricity over long distances.
visual_cues: Line of regularly spaced pylons, best seen through their long lattice shadows; a cleared corridor through forest; straight segments with angle towers at bends; lines converge at substations.

name: Electrical substation
description: A facility that switches electricity and changes its voltage.
visual_cues: Fenced gravel yard; rows of transformers and steel gantries; busbars; many transmission lines entering and leaving; small control building.

name: HVDC converter station
description: A facility that converts electricity between alternating and direct current at the ends of an HVDC link.
visual_cues: Very large windowless valve halls; outdoor AC filter yard with many small components; switchyard; DC line or cable leaving; often near coasts for subsea links.

name: Offshore substation
description: A platform that collects power from an offshore wind farm and sends it to shore.
visual_cues: Large rectangular topside on a jacket in the middle or edge of an offshore wind farm; helideck; bigger than any turbine foundation.

name: Iron ore mine
description: A mine, usually open-pit, that produces iron ore.
visual_cues: Large terraced pit, often in red or dark rock; haul roads; waste dumps; crushing and beneficiation plant; conveyors or a rail loop to load long ore trains; tailings dam.

name: Integrated steel plant (BF-BOF)
description: A plant that makes iron from ore in blast furnaces and turns it into steel.
visual_cues: Blast furnaces with round hot-blast stoves; long coke oven batteries; sinter plant; ore and coal stockyards; basic oxygen furnace shop; very long rolling mill buildings; slag heaps; often at a port with bulk-carrier berths.

name: Blast furnace
description: A tall furnace that smelts iron ore into molten iron using coke.
visual_cues: Round furnace structure with a conveyor or skip incline to its top; three or four cylindrical hot-blast stoves in a row beside it; dust catcher; cast house; usually part of an integrated steel plant.

name: Coke oven battery
description: A long block of ovens that bake coal into coke for blast furnaces.
visual_cues: Very long narrow rectangular block with a quenching tower and its plume at one end; coal tower; by-product plant with tanks; stacks; dark coal and coke piles nearby.

name: Electric arc furnace steel plant
description: A steel plant that melts scrap or direct reduced iron with electricity.
visual_cues: Large melt-shop building with a fume extraction system; scrap yard with piles and cranes; rolling mill building; no blast furnaces or coke ovens; large substation next to the plant.

name: Direct reduced iron plant
also_called: DRI plant; HBI plant; Midrex plant
description: A plant that turns iron ore pellets into iron using gas (or hydrogen) instead of coke.
visual_cues: Tall slender shaft-furnace tower; reformer with stacks; iron ore pellet stockpiles; conveyors; often next to an EAF plant or at a port.

name: Integrated cement plant
description: A plant that burns limestone in a kiln to make clinker and grinds it into cement.
visual_cues: Tall preheater tower next to a long thin rotary kiln; clinker cooler; round silos; limestone quarry nearby; conveyors; grey dust on surroundings.

name: Cement grinding plant
description: A plant that grinds clinker into cement, without its own kiln.
visual_cues: Mill buildings and several tall round silos; clinker storage; no preheater tower or kiln; often at ports or near cities.

name: Steam cracker (petrochemical plant)
description: A plant that breaks down ethane, naphtha or other feedstocks into ethylene, propylene and other chemicals.
visual_cues: Row of rectangular cracking furnaces with stacks; tall distillation columns; spheres and refrigerated tanks; large flare; extensive pipe racks; often beside a refinery or port.

name: Ammonia and fertiliser plant
also_called: fertiliser plant; urea plant; nitrogen plant
description: A plant that makes ammonia from natural gas or coal, often converting it to urea fertiliser.
visual_cues: Reformer and process units; tall cylindrical urea prilling tower or granulation unit; long product warehouses; refrigerated ammonia tanks; often a jetty.

name: Methanol plant
description: A plant that makes methanol from natural gas or coal.
visual_cues: Reformer or gasifiers with tall columns; product tanks; flares; coal-based plants also show coal yards and gasification towers.

name: Aluminium smelter
description: A plant that makes aluminium by electrolysis, using very large amounts of electricity.
visual_cues: Several extremely long parallel potline buildings (often over 1 km); round alumina silos; anode plant; large substation or captive power plant; often at a port.

name: Open-pit mine (other minerals)
description: A surface mine for metals or other minerals.
visual_cues: Large terraced pit in light or coloured rock; haul roads; waste rock dumps; processing plant and tailings dam nearby.

name: Tailings dam
description: An impoundment that stores fine waste from ore processing.
visual_cues: Large flat basin with a straight or terraced dam wall; grey, brown or coloured sediment and water; discharge pipes along the edge.

name: Data centre
description: A campus of buildings housing servers, a fast-growing user of electricity.
visual_cues: Large windowless rectangular buildings; rooftops covered with rows of cooling units; rows of backup generators along the walls; dedicated substation; often several identical buildings on one campus.

name: Railway track
description: A railway line for trains.
visual_cues: Thin continuous line with gentle curves (no sharp bends); ballast shows light grey; parallel tracks; bridges and level crossings; trains appear as long segmented lines.

name: Rail yard
description: An area with many parallel tracks where trains are sorted and stored.
visual_cues: Many parallel tracks fanning out from switches; stationary wagons; maintenance sheds; often near ports, mines and industrial sites.

name: Rail balloon loop
description: A loop of track that lets a whole train turn around while loading or unloading.
visual_cues: Oval or teardrop-shaped track loop, often around a stockpile or with a load-out silo; common at coal and iron ore mines, bulk terminals and coal power plants.

name: Highway
description: A major multi-lane road.
visual_cues: Wide road with a central divider; interchanges with ramps; overpasses; heavy traffic visible as small dots.

name: Airport
description: An airfield with runways for aircraft.
visual_cues: Long straight paved runways with markings; taxiways; aprons with parked aircraft; terminal buildings; fuel tank farm at large airports.

name: Overland conveyor
description: A long enclosed or open belt conveyor that moves bulk material.
visual_cues: Very thin straight line across the landscape (thinner than a road) with transfer towers at bends; links mines to plants, stockyards or jetties.

name: Jetty
description: A structure extending from the shore into water where ships berth.
visual_cues: Long narrow trestle running out to deeper water; a berthing head with mooring dolphins; pipework or a conveyor along the trestle; ships moored alongside.

name: Dry bulk terminal
description: A port facility for loading or unloading bulk cargoes such as ore, grain or coal.
visual_cues: Stockpiles or silos on the shore; conveyors to the berth; travelling ship loaders or grab unloaders; bulk carriers alongside.

name: Container port
description: A port terminal that handles shipping containers.
visual_cues: Large paved yard covered in colourful stacked rectangles; ship-to-shore cranes along the quay; container ships alongside; truck gates and rail sidings.

name: Single point mooring buoy
description: An offshore buoy where tankers moor to load or unload oil through hoses.
visual_cues: Small round buoy in open water with a tanker moored to it by a hawser; floating hoses; the tanker swings around the buoy with wind and current.

name: Breakwater
description: A barrier built into the sea to protect a harbour from waves.
visual_cues: Long rock or concrete structure, often curved, enclosing calm water; wave break visible on the seaward side.

name: Oil tanker
description: A ship that carries crude oil or refined products.
visual_cues: Long ship with a flat deck covered in pipework; cargo manifold in the middle of the deck; accommodation block and funnel at the stern; no cranes or hatches.

name: Bulk carrier
description: A ship that carries dry bulk cargo such as coal, ore or grain.
visual_cues: Long ship with a row of large rectangular hatch covers on deck; sometimes deck cranes between hatches; accommodation at the stern; seen at coal and ore terminals.

name: LPG / gas carrier
description: A ship that carries liquefied petroleum gas, ethane or ammonia.
visual_cues: Similar to a small oil tanker but with raised cylindrical or prismatic tank domes and less deck pipework; seen at refineries, crackers and gas terminals.
